title: Daily Life - High School Reunion
audio: mp3/287. Daily Life - High School Reunion.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
My name is Catherine and today we have an elementary level lesson in which we're going to talk about small talk.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们有一个初级课程，我们将在其中谈论闲聊。

segments.en: Today we're going to talk to an old friend and so we're going to give you some of the words and phrases you need to talk about your past or talk about how you have been.
segments.zh: 今天我们要和一个老朋友聊聊，所以会给你们一些单词和短语，用来谈论你的过去，或者聊聊你的近况。

segments.en: So let's listen to today's dialogue and we'll be back in a moment to discuss it.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听今天的对话，我们稍后会回来讨论它。

segments.en: I hate coming to high school reunions.
segments.zh: 我真不喜欢参加高中同学聚会。

segments.en: We will get to see your old classmates and catch up to see how they've been doing.
segments.zh: 能见见你的老同学，叙叙旧，了解一下他们的近况。
哦，看，那是罗伯特·马修斯。

segments.en: So Bill, how have you been?
We have two children who are in college and my business is going well.
segments.zh: 我们有两个正在上大学的孩子，我的生意进展顺利。
我是坚定的不婚主义者。

segments.en: I never married, although I do have a beautiful daughter with Mary.
segments.zh: 我从未结婚，虽然我和玛丽有一个漂亮的女儿。

segments.en: It didn't really work out between us, but I really can't complain either.
segments.zh: 我们俩最终没能走到一起，不过我也真没什么好抱怨的。

segments.en: I was hoping he would come tonight.
Nah, I'm just janking your chain.
I was hoping he would show up.
So now let's get started with our language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们开始我们的语言要点。

segments.en: The first phrase we have here in language takeaway is a very important one because it is the setting for today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 我们在语言要点里的第一个短语非常重要，因为它是今天对话的场景。

segments.en: We are at a high school reunion.
segments.zh: 我们正在参加高中同学聚会。

segments.en: So everyone knows what high school is, but a high school reunion is when you go back to your high school for a party maybe five years or ten years after you graduate.
segments.zh: 所以每个人都知道高中是什么，但高中同学聚会是指毕业五年或十年后，你回到高中参加的一场聚会。

segments.en: So then you meet all your old friends from high school.
segments.zh: 那么你会遇到所有高中的老朋友。

segments.en: You talk about how you have been and just meet up with everyone that maybe you haven't seen in a very long time.
segments.zh: 你聊聊彼此的近况，和那些可能很久没见过的人见见面。

segments.en: So a reunion usually happens every five years, ten years, or twenty years.
segments.zh: 因此，重聚通常每五年、十年或二十年举行一次。

segments.en: It can happen at different times, but this is important because you can have many different kinds of reunions like a college reunion or a high school reunion.
segments.zh: 它可能发生在不同的时间，但这很重要，因为你可以有许多不同类型的重聚，比如大学聚会或高中同学聚会。

segments.en: I've even heard of some people who had an elementary school reunion.
segments.zh: 我甚至听说过有人办小学同学聚会。

segments.en: Imagine seeing your classmates when you were maybe ten years old.
segments.zh: 想象一下，在你十岁的时候看到你的同学。

segments.en: Alright so we're at a high school reunion and we are there because we're going to meet our old classmates and to catch up and see how they have been.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们在高中同学聚会上，我们来这儿是为了见见老同学，叙叙旧，看看他们过得怎么样。

segments.en: Okay so this is exactly what you do at a reunion.
segments.zh: 好吧，这正是你在重聚时所做的。

segments.en: You catch up with people that you maybe lost touch with, to catch up means to find out about what people have been doing since the last time you talked.
segments.zh: 你会和可能失去联系的人叙叙旧，catch up 的意思是了解自上次交谈以来大家一直在做什么。

segments.en: So maybe Marco and I were classmates in high school and we haven't talked in ten years.
segments.zh: 所以也许马可和我在高中时是同学，我们已经十年没有说话了。

segments.en: I say, Marco, I want to catch up.
segments.zh: 我说，马可，我想跟你叙叙旧。

segments.en: I want to learn about what you do, who you married, where you work, things like that.
segments.zh: 我想了解你做什么工作、跟谁结了婚、在哪里上班，诸如此类。

segments.en: Right, so when two people get together to catch up, maybe it doesn't even have to be a very long time.
segments.zh: 对，所以当两个人聚在一起叙旧时，也许并不一定是很久没见。

segments.en: Maybe you haven't seen your friend for a week and so you want to get together, have a cup of coffee and catch up and see how the relationship has been going or how it works so you want to catch up.
segments.zh: 也许你一个星期没见朋友了，于是想聚一聚，喝杯咖啡，聊聊近况，看看彼此关系怎么样、过得如何，所以你想叙叙旧。

segments.en: So you can say this in a very simple way, let's catch up or it's been nice to catch up.
segments.zh: 所以你可以用很简单的方式说，比如 let's catch up，或者 it's been nice to catch up。

segments.en: Alright, moving on to our next word.
segments.zh: 好吧，继续我们的下一个词。

segments.en: This guy Bill meets up with Robert Matthews and they're saying, hey, wow, great to see you and he answers by saying, likewise.
segments.zh: 比尔这个人遇到了罗伯特·马修斯，他们说'嘿，哇，很高兴见到你'，他回答说 likewise。

segments.en: So it's good to see you, likewise.
segments.zh: 所以'很高兴见到你'，回答 likewise 就行。

segments.en: That means it's good to see you too.
segments.zh: 这意味着很高兴见到你。

segments.en: So you don't have to repeat everything that person just said.
segments.zh: 所以你不必重复那个人刚才所说的一切。

segments.en: For example, if I just meet someone new and I say it's a pleasure to meet you, you can say?
segments.zh: 例如，如果我只是认识一个新人并且我说很高兴见到你，你可以说？

segments.en: Because I don't want to say it's a pleasure to meet you too.
segments.zh: 因为我不想把'也很高兴认识你'整句说出来。

segments.en: So likewise is a very short way to say all of those things.
segments.zh: 所以 likewise 是表达所有这些话的简短方式。

segments.en: So we were finding out about Robert Matthews and he says that, well, he is a dedicated bachelor.
segments.zh: 所以我们了解了罗伯特·马修斯的情况，他说，嗯，他是个铁了心的单身汉。

segments.en: So a dedicated bachelor, what is a bachelor, Marco?
segments.zh: 那么铁了心的单身汉，什么是单身汉，马可？

segments.en: So a bachelor is a person who is not married, a person who is single.
segments.zh: 所以单身汉是一个未婚的人，一个单身的人。

segments.en: A woman cannot be a bachelor.
So a bachelor is specifically a man and he's not married and we often have a stereotype, that means we have an idea of what a bachelor lives like.
segments.zh: 所以单身汉特别是一个男人，他没有结婚，我们经常有刻板印象，这意味着我们知道单身汉的生活方式。

segments.en: He has only beer in his refrigerator and he has many relationships and no wife.
segments.zh: 他的冰箱里只有啤酒，他有很多人际关系，没有妻子。

segments.en: So a dedicated bachelor is a person who is not married and doesn't really seem to want to get married or any of this.
segments.zh: 所以铁了心的单身汉就是没结婚、而且看起来并不打算结婚或搞这一套的人。

segments.en: And well, to finish off, this guy Robert lied a little bit to Bill saying that Frank had passed away.
segments.zh: 好吧，最后，罗伯特这家伙跟比尔撒了个小谎，说弗兰克已经去世了。

segments.en: That's really mean, but this phrase to pass away is very important and something we should talk about.
segments.zh: 这真的很卑鄙，但这个短语非常重要，我们应该谈谈。

segments.en: So what does it mean to pass away?
segments.zh: 那么逝世是什么意思呢？

segments.en: It's another way of saying he died.
segments.zh: 这是另一种说法，他死了。

segments.en: Yeah, it's a lot more subtle and nicer.
segments.zh: 是的，这样说更委婉，也更好听。

segments.en: So instead of saying Frank died, you say Frank passed away.
segments.zh: 因此，与其说弗兰克死了，不如说弗兰克去世了。

segments.en: So you could say, you know, last year my grandmother passed away.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，你知道，去年我的祖母去世了。

segments.en: That's a way of saying that my grandmother died last year, but again, it's a lot nicer way to say that.
segments.zh: 这是一种说法，我的祖母去年去世了，但同样，这是一个更好的说法。

segments.en: Yeah, because the word died can be a little bit too direct and too harsh.
segments.zh: 是的，因为这个词可能有点过于直接和过于苛刻。

segments.en: So maybe saying my grandmother passed away last year, it's a nicer way of saying it.
segments.zh: 所以也许说我的祖母去年去世了，这是一种更好的说法。

segments.en: So that's all the language takeaway you have.
segments.zh: 这就是你所有的语言要点。

segments.en: Let's take a look at our dialogue again and we'll be back.
segments.zh: 让我们再看看我们的对话，我们会回来的。

segments.en: I hate coming to high school reunions.
segments.zh: 我真不喜欢参加高中同学聚会。

segments.en: We will get to see your old classmates and catch up to see how they've been doing.
segments.zh: 能见见你的老同学，叙叙旧，了解一下他们的近况。
哦，看，那是罗伯特·马修斯。

segments.en: So Bill, how have you been?
We have two children who are in college and my business is going well.
segments.zh: 我们有两个正在上大学的孩子，我的生意进展顺利。
我是坚定的不婚主义者。

segments.en: I never married, although I do have a beautiful daughter with Mary.
segments.zh: 我从未结婚，虽然我和玛丽有一个漂亮的女儿。

segments.en: It didn't really work out between us, but I really can't complain either.
segments.zh: 我们俩最终没能走到一起，不过我也真没什么好抱怨的。

segments.en: I was hoping he would come tonight.
Nah, I'm just janking your chain.
He told me he would show up.
Alright let's move on now to four key phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们现在继续讨论关于流利表达的四个关键短语。

segments.en: So the focus of today's Fluency Builder is small talk.
segments.zh: 所以今天流利表达的重点是闲聊。

segments.en: These are phrases you can use when you're at a reunion or a dinner, especially with people you don't know very well.
segments.zh: 这些是您在聚会或晚餐时可以使用的短语，尤其是与您不太了解的人在一起。

segments.en: So let's jump in and look at this first phrase.
segments.zh: 所以让我们跳进去看看第一个短语。

segments.en: So he says, hey Bill, wow, great to see you.
segments.zh: 所以他说，嘿，比尔，哇，很高兴见到你。

segments.en: So this is a nice little opening phrase saying, wow, I'm really excited to see you.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个很好的开场白，说，哇，我真的很高兴见到你。

segments.en: I'm really happy to see you.
You say this at the beginning of a conversation.
segments.zh: 你在谈话开始时这么说。

segments.en: And actually Bill responded by saying likewise.
He's saying, wow, great to see you too.
Then he continues by saying, it's been a long time.
segments.zh: 然后他继续说，已经很久了。

segments.en: This means that these two people, they have not seen each other in a very long time.
segments.zh: 这意味着这两个人，他们已经很久没有见面了。

segments.en: You can also say, it's been so long or it's been a long time.
segments.zh: 你也可以说，已经很久了，或者已经很长时间了。

segments.en: That means it's been a long time since we last saw each other.
segments.zh: 这意味着我们上次见面已经很久了。

segments.en: So Robert goes on to ask Bill.
segments.zh: 所以罗伯特继续问比尔。

segments.en: He says, well, you know, how have you been?
segments.zh: 他说，嗯，你知道，你最近怎么样？

segments.en: Bill answers by saying, can't complain.
segments.zh: 比尔回答说：没什么可抱怨的。

segments.en: So this is not grammatically correct.
segments.zh: 所以这在语法上是不正确的。

segments.en: But when we're speaking in English and we're having a conversation like this, it's okay to say just can't complain as a phrase.
segments.zh: 但是当我们在说英语、进行这样的对话时，只说 can't complain 当作一个短语是可以的。

segments.en: So he's saying, how have you been?
segments.zh: 所以他说，你最近怎么样？

segments.en: That means nothing bad has happened.
segments.zh: 这意味着没有发生任何不好的事情。

segments.en: You're saying that things are good.
They're not fantastic, but they're not bad either.
segments.zh: 它们并不出色，但它们也不错。

segments.en: So it's just a phrase where very directly you can say, oh, can't complain.
segments.zh: 所以这就是个短语，你可以很直接地说，哦，can't complain。

segments.en: So you could even say this about other things.
segments.zh: 所以你甚至可以说其他事情。

segments.en: Like, you know, I asked John how his job was and he said, can't complain.
segments.zh: 比如，你知道，我问约翰工作怎么样，他说，没什么可抱怨的。

segments.en: It's not great, but it's not bad.
And obviously we saw how Robert lied to Bill by saying that their good friend, that their good friend Frank had passed away.
segments.zh: 显然，我们看到罗伯特如何对比尔撒谎，说他们的好朋友弗兰克已经去世了。

segments.en: And he said, are you serious?
No, I'm just yanking your chain.
Okay, so this might sound very strange to a lot of you because a chain is something that doesn't really seem to fit in this conversation.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这对你们中的很多人来说可能听起来很奇怪，因为链条似乎并不真正适合这次谈话。

segments.en: But yanking your chain, remember this as a phrase, it means I'm just joking.
segments.zh: 但是 yank your chain，把它当短语记住，意思是'我只是在开玩笑'。

segments.en: I'm lying to you, I guess.
So, but how can you use this in another context?
segments.zh: 那么，你怎么在别的语境里用它呢？

segments.en: I could say, you know what, Marco, I have something I have to tell you.
segments.zh: 我可以说，你知道吗，马可，我有话要告诉你。

segments.en: No, I'm just yanking your chain.

segments.zh: 或者不，我只是在开玩笑。

segments.en: So you're kind of teasing someone when you do this, right?
segments.zh: 所以当你这样做时，你有点在取笑某人，对吧？

segments.en: I'm making you believe something that isn't true.
segments.zh: 我让你相信一些不真实的东西。

segments.en: So this is something you can use after you tell someone that you were just joking.
segments.zh: 所以这是你可以在告诉别人你只是在开玩笑之后使用的东西。

segments.en: So I'm just yanking your chain.
You can't translate it directly or literally because it's not going to make sense.
segments.zh: 你不能直接或逐字翻译它，因为那样讲不通。

segments.en: So just remember this as a phrasal verb or a phrase in general.
segments.zh: 所以请记住这是一个短语动词或一个短语。

segments.en: Let's listen to our dialogue one last time and we'll be back to talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 让我们最后一次听我们的对话，我们会回来多说一点。

segments.en: I hate coming to high school reunions.
segments.zh: 我真不喜欢参加高中同学聚会。

segments.en: We will get to see your old classmates and catch up to see how they've been doing.
segments.zh: 能见见你的老同学，叙叙旧，了解一下他们的近况。
哦，看，那是罗伯特·马修斯。

segments.en: So Bill, how have you been?
We have two children who are in college and my business is going well.
segments.zh: 我们有两个正在上大学的孩子，我的生意进展顺利。
我是坚定的不婚主义者。

segments.en: I never married, although I do have a beautiful daughter with Mary.
segments.zh: 我从未结婚，虽然我和玛丽有一个漂亮的女儿。

segments.en: It didn't really work out between us, but I really can't complain either.
segments.zh: 我们俩最终没能走到一起，不过我也真没什么好抱怨的。

segments.en: I was hoping he would come tonight.
Nah, I'm just janking your chain.
He told me he would show up.
All right, so we're back and talking about high school reunions.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们回来谈论高中聚会。

segments.en: These are very popular in the United States, right?
segments.zh: 这些在美国很受欢迎，对吧？

segments.en: They are very popular and I think people often have them every five, ten, fifteen, twenty years, but most people don't go to the high school reunion until either ten or twenty years after their high school graduation.
segments.zh: 它们很受欢迎，我觉得人们常常是每五年、十年、十五年、二十年办一次，但大多数人要到高中毕业十年或二十年后才会去参加高中同学聚会。

segments.en: I think five years is very soon.

Ten years is nice because you haven't seen people, but twenty years is really, I think, shocking because people can be completely different or they could be the same, but it's been, you know, you were eighteen when you graduated high school.
segments.zh: 十年挺好的，因为你已经很久没见过大家了；但我觉得二十年真的很让人震惊，因为人可能变得完全不一样，也可能一点没变，可你知道，高中毕业时你才十八岁。
现在你已经三十八岁了。

segments.en: You have this whole life that you've had and so I think it's much more interesting.
segments.zh: 你已经过了整整一段人生，所以我觉得这有意思多了。

segments.en: Yeah, it's very interesting and I guess people go to these things half because they do want to maybe meet up with old friends that they haven't kept in touch with.
segments.zh: 是的，这很有趣。我想人们参加这种活动，一半是因为确实想见见那些没保持联系的老朋友。

segments.en: I think especially this was very popular before the whole internet revolution.
segments.zh: 我认为尤其是在整个互联网革命之前，这非常受欢迎。

segments.en: Now everyone's in touch on Facebook and emails and it's just so much easier to keep in touch, but before you have to remember that it was basically by telephone or by mail, so actually seeing a person ten years or catching up with them was very difficult back then.
segments.zh: 现在大家都能通过 Facebook 和邮件联系，保持联系容易多了；但别忘了，以前基本上只能靠电话或信件，所以在当年，真正见一个人或跟他叙叙旧是非常困难的。

segments.en: Yeah, we all see photos and videos now of our classmates, so it's not quite as surprising when we bump into them later, but I think it is still interesting though because at least on my social networking websites there are a lot of people that I don't have connections to, and so I look forward to my high school reunion when I get to see some of these people and kind of find out what they've been doing for the past ten or fifteen years.
segments.zh: 是的，我们现在都能看到同学们的照片和视频，所以以后再碰到他们时就没那么惊讶了，不过我觉得这仍然很有趣，因为至少在我的社交网站上，有很多和我没有联系的人，所以我期待着我的高中同学聚会，到时候能见到其中一些人，了解他们过去十年或十五年都在做什么。

segments.en: It's actually very interesting I guess when you see how your classmates have changed, how maybe the one that used to be the nerd or maybe not very attractive all of a sudden is really attractive and has like a supermodel as a wife or how these things work out.
segments.zh: 我想，看到同学们发生了怎样的变化其实很有趣，比如以前那个书呆子、或者长得不怎么样的人，突然变得很有魅力，还娶了个像超模一样的妻子，或者事情就是这么发展。

segments.en: Or the high school football captain is now kind of sad and fat.
segments.zh: 或者当年的高中橄榄球队队长现在又惨又胖。

segments.en: So yeah, these are the types of surprises that people look forward to when they go to high school reunions.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，这些是人们在参加高中聚会时所期待的惊喜类型。
总之，这是个非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: Let us know on our website EnglishPod.com if your high school and the place where you live, do they have high school reunions or maybe even elementary school reunions.
segments.zh: 告诉我们，你所在的地方、你的高中会不会办高中同学聚会，甚至小学同学聚会。可以在我们网站 EnglishPod.com 上留言。

segments.en: We hope to find out more about you guys' experiences and until next time.
segments.zh: 我们希望了解更多关于你们的经历，直到下一次。
